prompt.context_jp: ホテル前まで戻ってきた高橋の前に、どこからともなく岸本___滑り込んできた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ホテル前まで戻ってきた高橋の前に、どこからともなく岸本___滑り込んできた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits best.

feedback.correct_en: Kishimoto appears unexpectedly here — this is new information entering the scene, so が marks him as the newly-introduced subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would signal Kishimoto as an already-established topic, but he's suddenly 'sliding in from nowhere,' which is a classic new-information context.

contrast_examples.jp: どこからともなく男が現れた。
contrast_examples.en: A man appeared out of nowhere.

contrast_examples.jp: その男は黙って立っていた。

prompt.context_jp: 「えっ はっち 何言ったの？」への返答
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___自分の特殊能力(のことを話した)。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle. (Context: others said different things; what did YOU say?)

feedback.correct_en: は marks contrastive topic — 'as for me (as opposed to the others), I talked about my special ability.' The conversation is comparing what each person said.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present '私' as new/exhaustive subject, but here the speaker is contrasting herself with the others who were also interviewed.

contrast_examples.jp: 私は英語を話す、彼は中国語を話す。
contrast_examples.en: I speak English; he speaks Chinese. (contrastive は)
It was I who spoke. (exhaustive が)

prompt.context_jp: (前の人は松山千春を選んだ流れで)
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___もう 内容っていうより 英語の歌にします。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle. (She contrasts her choice with the previous person's.)

feedback.correct_en: は sets up contrast with the previous speaker's answer: 'As for me (unlike her), I'd pick an English song.' Classic contrastive-topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would wrongly assert 'I (and only I) will choose' as new info, missing the comparison-with-others feel of the conversation.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は和食、私は洋食にする。
contrast_examples.en: He'll have Japanese; I'll have Western.

prompt.context_jp: 章の冒頭
prompt.prompt_jp: 富士浅田の夜___更けかけたころ、テレビ局の岸本と松崎は路上の隅に車を止めた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the opening scene-setter.

feedback.correct_en: In a subordinate 'when X happened' clause describing a new scene, が marks the subject as fresh descriptive information — standard for 〜が更ける.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn 'the night' into a topic ('as for the night...'), awkward for a scene-setting temporal clause.

prompt.context_jp: 高橋はうつむいたまま、
prompt.prompt_jp: ふだんの飄々とした調子___、そこにはなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: は contrasts 'his usual carefree tone' (which should be there) with the current moment — contrastive/topical は fits perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present it as neutral new information, losing the implied 'unlike usual' nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: いつもの笑顔はなかった。
contrast_examples.en: His usual smile wasn't there (contrast with usual).

prompt.context_jp: フロントの常連客について
prompt.prompt_jp: 宮本さん___、また違う女の人連れてましたね。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Miyamoto is a known regular customer — a familiar topic. は flags him as the topic of gossip.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce him as new information, but Yumi and Kiyomi both already know who he is.

contrast_examples.jp: 田中さんは今日休みです。

prompt.context_jp: 高橋が岸本に
prompt.prompt_jp: この力___なかったら、あなた今死んでましたよね。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in the conditional clause.

feedback.correct_en: In 〜がなかったら conditionals, が marks the existence/absence subject neutrally. 'If this power didn't exist...'
feedback.incorrect_en: は in this subordinate conditional would sound unnatural; existential 'ある/ない' clauses typically take が.

contrast_examples.jp: お金がなかったら困る。
contrast_examples.en: If I had no money, I'd be in trouble.

contrast_examples.jp: お金はないけど幸せだ。
contrast_examples.en: I have no money, but I'm happy. (contrastive は)

prompt.context_jp: 高橋のセリフ
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___あなたの命を救ったんですから、あなたも私の生活のジャマをしないでください。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: は contrasts '私' with 'あなた' in the following clause ('I did X, so you do Y'). This is the classic parallel-contrast は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like exhaustive identification ('I'm the one who saved you'), losing the balanced I/you contrast that drives the sentence.

prompt.context_jp: 窓の外に高橋を見かけて
prompt.prompt_jp: あっ、高橋さん___!
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for a sudden sighting.

feedback.correct_en: 'あっ、Xだ！' is the natural shape for pointing out something you just noticed — 'Oh, it's Takahashi!'
feedback.incorrect_en: '高橋さんは' would need a predicate ('Takahashi is...'); it doesn't work as a standalone 'oh look!' exclamation.

prompt.context_jp: 事故の瞬間
prompt.prompt_jp: 走ってきた車の前に、岸本の体___投げ出された。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: A dramatic, sudden event where '岸本の体' is new/focal information in the scene — が marks the subject of a reported happening.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would topicalize his body, which doesn't suit the sudden, event-reporting narration.

prompt.context_jp: 松山千春の歌について
prompt.prompt_jp: スケールの大きさで、テレビ盗んだこと___ちっぽけなことのように思わせる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: '〜を思わせる' uses が for the subject of the embedded clause: '(it makes you think that) stealing a TV is a trivial thing.' The subject-marker for the trivial-feeling idea is が.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would double up with the following thought-object; here テレビ盗んだこと is the subject of 'ちっぽけに思える'-type feel, needing が.

prompt.context_jp: 高橋の説明
prompt.prompt_jp: 俺もう無視して行こうとしたんだけどさ、結構しつこくて___。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking contrast with his attempt to ignore.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence ends with explanatory ね after けど — the contrast is already carried by けど. 'I tried to ignore him, but he was really persistent, you know.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が as a final particle doesn't fit here; the clause structure 〜けど、〜て already handles the contrast.

contrast_examples.jp: 行こうとしたけど、無理でね。
contrast_examples.en: I tried to go, but it was no good, you see.

contrast_examples.jp: 行こうとしたが無理だった。
contrast_examples.en: I tried to go, but it was no good.

prompt.context_jp: 元夫から養育費をもらっている話
prompt.prompt_jp: 元夫から毎月養育費をもらって___いるけど、だからって余裕があるわけではない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 〜てはいるけど is a set contrastive pattern: 'I do receive it, BUT...' は inserted into the て-form flags the concessive contrast.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜ているけど without は works grammatically, but the blank specifically calls for the contrastive-emphasis は that highlights the 'yes, but' feel.

contrast_examples.jp: 知ってはいるけど、言わない。
contrast_examples.en: I DO know, but I won't say.

contrast_examples.jp: 知っているけど言わない。

prompt.context_jp: 岸本と松崎
prompt.prompt_jp: 路上の隅___車を止め、目当ての相手を待っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: With 止める (to park/stop a vehicle), に marks the stopping-point/destination where the car comes to rest.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark the location of an action; but 止める focuses on the resting location, which Japanese treats as a に-point.

contrast_examples.en: I parked the car in the lot.

prompt.context_jp: 高橋の脅し
prompt.prompt_jp: あなたの身___不幸が起こるかもしれませんよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 〜に起こる marks the person/place where an event happens to someone. 'Misfortune may happen TO you.'
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks the location of an action but 起こる (to occur/befall) attaches with に when something befalls a person.

contrast_examples.jp: そこで事件が起こった。

prompt.context_jp: 高橋が記者に
prompt.prompt_jp: これ以上___のやめてもらえませんか？迷惑なんだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that fits.

feedback.correct_en: 付きまとう specifically means 'to follow/pester persistently,' which fits a reporter who won't leave someone alone.
feedback.incorrect_en: 追いかける is just 'to chase'; 見つける is 'to find.' Neither captures the clingy, nuisance-like persistence that 迷惑 implies.

contrast_examples.jp: 記者に付きまとわれる。
contrast_examples.en: To be stalked/pestered by a reporter.

prompt.context_jp: 清美「バッチリ___ときました」
prompt.prompt_jp: バッチリ___ときました。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb — Kiyomi successfully covered for Takahashi.

feedback.correct_en: ごまかす = to fool/deceive/dodge a question. Kiyomi deflected the reporter's inquiry — 'I covered it up perfectly.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 忘れる (forget) doesn't match the active deception. 隠す (hide) is close, but ごまかす specifically fits dodging questions.

prompt.context_jp: 髪ボサボサのインタビューについて
prompt.prompt_jp: あれが全国で放送されんの___んだけど。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word.

feedback.correct_en: キツイ in casual speech means 'rough/tough to handle emotionally' — perfect for 'cringe at the thought.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 痛い (painful) and 硬い (hard) don't carry the 'emotionally unbearable/embarrassing' nuance that キツイ does in colloquial use.

prompt.context_jp: 新座の皮肉
prompt.prompt_jp: データが消えちゃうのも___ってことだよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the phrase.

feedback.correct_en: 実力のうち = 'part of your (own) ability/skill.' A sarcastic idiom: 'Even losing the data counts as part of your ability.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 運のうち or 仕事のうち aren't fixed expressions here; the specific sarcastic idiom is 〜も実力のうち.

contrast_examples.en: Luck is part of ability too.
This is part of the job too.

prompt.context_jp: カットを頼みに行くのが恥ずかしい理由
prompt.prompt_jp: なんか___だと思われそうじゃん。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word.

feedback.correct_en: 自意識過剰 = 'overly self-conscious,' exactly the fear of being seen as caring too much about one's own appearance on TV.
feedback.incorrect_en: 自信過剰 means 'overconfident' (about ability); 過保護 is 'overprotective (of someone else).' Neither matches worrying how YOU look.

prompt.context_jp: 高橋の警戒
prompt.prompt_jp: これ、下手すると___案件だよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word.

feedback.correct_en: 報道案件 = 'news/press matter.' Takahashi worries this could escalate into actual journalism coverage, not just a tabloid clip.
feedback.incorrect_en: 広告 (ad) or 販売 (sales) don't fit — the fear is specifically about news reporting on him.

contrast_examples.en: It might become a news story.
To take on an ad project.

prompt.context_jp: ガンプラ作りの話
prompt.prompt_jp: ___とこでやめようと思ったんだけど、___とこが見当たんなくてさ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the phrase.

feedback.correct_en: キリのいい = 'a good stopping/breaking point.' A fixed collocation about finding a natural place to stop.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other options aren't idiomatic in Japanese. キリ(切り) specifically refers to a cutoff/break in work.

contrast_examples.jp: キリのいいところで休もう。
contrast_examples.en: Let's rest at a good stopping point.

prompt.context_jp: 岸本の証言
prompt.prompt_jp: 何なら___くらいのスピードだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word for Takahashi's unbelievable speed.

feedback.correct_en: 瞬間移動 = teleportation. Kishimoto describes the speed as 'practically teleportation,' matching the sci-fi exaggeration.
feedback.incorrect_en: 高速道路 is a highway (noun, not a speed); 時間旅行 is time travel, which is about time not movement speed.

contrast_examples.jp: 瞬間移動したみたいだ。

prompt.context_jp: 記者が付きまとうシーン
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural as the reporter's reassurance to Takahashi?

choices.text: 決して悪いようにはしないんで。
絶対に悪いことをしないんで。

feedback.correct_en: 悪いようにはしない is a set polite-reassurance idiom meaning 'I won't do you dirty / I'll treat you fairly.' That's the natural pitch here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 悪いことをしない literally means 'I won't do bad things,' which sounds like a child promising to behave, not a reporter reassuring a source.

contrast_examples.jp: 悪いようにはしないから任せて。
contrast_examples.en: I won't do you wrong, so trust me.

prompt.context_jp: 高橋のつっこみ
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural as Takahashi's exasperated response to Kiyomi making him guess?

choices.text: この空気で それクイズにする？
この雰囲気の中で それをクイズにしますか？

feedback.correct_en: The casual, slightly flat 'この空気で それクイズにする？' matches their familiar coworker banter — short, with dropped particles.
feedback.incorrect_en: The B version is grammatically fine but too formal and padded for close coworkers in a tense moment — it kills the comic timing.

contrast_examples.en: You're turning that into a quiz? (casual)

contrast_examples.jp: それをクイズになさいますか。
contrast_examples.en: Will you make that into a quiz? (overly formal)

prompt.context_jp: 清美が由美の噂話を遮る
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural for cutting off Yumi's gossip?

choices.text: ごめんね あの… 今 それ どうでもいいわ。
すみません。現在、その話題は重要ではありません。

feedback.correct_en: The casual A matches Kiyomi softly brushing aside gossip from a junior coworker — colloquial and warm.
feedback.incorrect_en: The B version sounds like a corporate announcement; no coworker would phrase 'that's not important right now' like that in a casual exchange.

contrast_examples.jp: 今それどうでもいいわ。
現在それは重要ではありません。
contrast_examples.en: That is not of importance at present. (stiff)

prompt.context_jp: 友達同士での提案
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural when suggesting they go ask the reporter to cut their part?

choices.text: てかさ、うちらの部分 カットしてくださいって 言いに行く？
ところで、私たちの部分をカットしていただくようお願いしに参りますか？

feedback.correct_en: Among close friends, うちら/てかさ/言いに行く? is the natural casual register. The quoted 〜してください stays inside the request itself.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses humble/polite forms (いただく, 参る) between best friends, which sounds absurdly formal for the café scene.

contrast_examples.jp: ちょっと言いに行こうよ。
申し上げに参りましょう。
contrast_examples.en: Let us go to humbly say. (way too formal)

prompt.context_jp: フロントでカードキーを渡す
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural at a hotel front desk?

choices.text: こちら カードキーでございます。ごゆっくりお過ごしくださいませ。
これ カードキーです。ゆっくりしてください。

feedback.correct_en: Hotel service register demands こちら/でございます/ごゆっくり〜くださいませ — the standard set phrases guests expect at check-in.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is grammatically fine but far too plain for a hotel; it sounds like handing a key to a friend, not a paying guest.

contrast_examples.jp: ごゆっくりお過ごしくださいませ。
